blocking.problem: §17.1 requires every access to lie wholly in one live allocation. TDL-4 puts distinct globals and coherent heap objects into one arena, while §16.3 removes their individual global entries and §16.4 checks only the ISA allocation containing the address. ISA §7.2 gives the whole coh interface region one pinned live entry. Thus logical object bounds and liveness disappear. Use the arena-o1 layout with two distinct one-byte globals at offsets 0 and 1, containing 01 and 02. A slice performing load i16 at offset 0 must fault 7: neither global contains both bytes. The specified boundscheck/load rows instead succeed with 513. I reproduced this by adapting arena-o1 in an anonymous memory file, updating its hashes, and running the supplied interpreter: check accepted; run-oracle with coh=0102, arg=0 and budget=100,0,32,1 returned code=0, payload=513, steps=7. Arena padding and freed coherent allocations have the same missing validation. This is a dialect-to-ISA mapping defect, not an ISA gap.
blocking.fix: In TDL-4 and §16.4 state: "The arena interface range is storage, not a logical allocation. Maintain the base, size and live state of each arena object. Before every program-memory access of n bytes at p, require that the entire nonwrapping range [p,p+n) lies in one live logical allocation; otherwise produce fault 7 before the access. The pinned coh entry does not satisfy this logical check." Use an ordinary materialised runtime helper over this metadata as the default, with its rows charged in the reference object; apply the same validation to event-producing stores and gate their mutation on success. Include coherent allocator allocation/free updates and metadata transfer in the contract. Retain one physical coh region so superposed addressing remains available. Correct witness: the spanning i16 load gives payload=0/code=7, whereas either separate i8 load succeeds with 1 or 2.

blocking.problem: §8.5 promises a private copy of the caller's whole memory and allocator state, but R is still selected from objects the closure may load; "if R is empty, no transfer runs". Allocation primitives read hidden allocator state without an LLVM load. Consider a caller that has allocated 16 bytes at heap_base=4096 and then invokes a materialised oracle consisting only of p=__bennett_nz_alloc(1); return ptrtoint(p). It has no load, global or shadow-stack use, so R is empty and its reference object starts with heap_used=0. It returns 4096; the promised call-entry-state execution returns 4112. With heap budget 16, the inherited-state execution must instead fault 2, while the fresh-heap map succeeds. The stack-adoption fix does not cover this allocation-only closure. Reusing a snapshot solely because no store to R occurred can also miss intervening alloc/free operations.
blocking.fix: In §8.5 state: "Allocation, deallocation and allocation-validity checks read allocator metadata even when the closure contains no LLVM load. Treat that metadata as an entry-state dependency. Replay the caller's allocation history and live bits whenever those operations can execute, independently of the byte read set; an empty byte read set does not permit resetting allocator state. Snapshot reuse requires unchanged dependent allocation metadata as well as unchanged dependent bytes." Default to replaying the complete allocation table for any closure with such a dependency; bytes may still be omitted when unread. Add the allocation-only witness: after the caller's 16-byte allocation, sufficient-budget payload=4112/code=0, and heap budget 16 gives payload=0/code=2. Neither oracle invocation changes the caller's allocation state.

blocking.problem: The compute-specific recorder fix leaves ordinary nested generations inconsistent. TDL-2 checks enclosing recorders for Co writes, but a Cl byte is still "the shadow updated by the recorder's own classical events". Parent events have not been applied while the parent recorder is active (§18.2). Witness: t starts Cl(0); outer f stores 9 to t and calls ctrl(c2,g), where g flips target z iff t==9; invoke f under c1, with both controls equal to 1 and z=0. The child has no own write to t, K(t) is still Cl, and the parent's unpredicated xmask is not a Co write. The literal child view reads shadow 0, so it omits the flip. The sequential branch semantics promised by TDL-2/§18.4 reads the parent's 9 and flips z. The new retained-recorder sentence applies to compute, not this nested ctrl.
blocking.fix: Replace the Cl-view sentence in TDL-2 with: "A child generation inherits the invoking generation's current speculative view. A Cl byte is obtained by applying the visible enclosing recorders' classical updates in execution order, then the child's own updates, to the invocation-entry shadow. The enclosing invocation control is not added to that inherited view until event composition. Co writes remain Co, and sibling branch recorders remain isolated until the join." Apply this to nested ctrl, adj and compute consistently with branch-local views. Add the witness with expected events xmask t+0 0x09 ctrl c1; x z ctrl c1 c2. For c1=c2=1 the final t is 9 and z is 1; for c1=0 both remain zero.

blocking.section: §12.2 n-defined-zero; §12.4 V4 and validator-v4-clean; §12.8 N27; Appendix C
blocking.problem: The new examples contradict the existing materialisation boundary. N27 explicitly replaces ctlz and cttz with __bennett_rt_<name>_i<W> calls; Appendix C assigns them to N27; V4 rejects any intrinsic N27 removes. Nevertheless n-defined-zero's full normalise-out retains both LLVM intrinsics, and validator-v4-clean says "ctlz with false is retained" and requires accept for a residual llvm.ctlz.i8 call. A validator following V4 rejects that exact positive example; one following the example accepts it. §16.4 also has no retained ctlz row. Correctly setting the N12 poison flag is an intermediate step, not the specified full N27 output.
blocking.fix: Keep N27 and add to §12.2/§12.4: "N12 totalises the flag before N27; it does not exempt abs, ctlz or cttz from their later expansion. Full materialised output contains no calls to these LLVM intrinsics, including false-flag calls." Change n-defined-zero's output calls to %a = call i8 @__bennett_rt_ctlz_i8(i8 %x, i1 false) and %b = call i8 @__bennett_rt_cttz_i8(i8 %x, i1 false), with matching runtime declarations/definitions; the add and returns remain unchanged. Give validator-v4-clean the materialised helper form, and make residual ctlz(false) a negative V4 witness alongside ctlz(true). Expected f(0)=16 and f(1)=7 remain unchanged. Alternatively retaining these intrinsics requires changing N27, V4, Appendix C and adding a canonical §16 row; I would keep the existing runtime-expansion design.

summary: Revise, including core. All 32 prior blockers are resolved in their originally reported cases; previous_status records each individually. The V10 correction is also consistent with the retained FP-carrier contract. Four S0 findings remain: lost arena object bounds, missing allocator-only entry dependencies, missing enclosing classical-view updates in nested generation, and contradictory new ctlz/cttz witnesses. The arena witness was checked and executed with the supplied ISA interpreter using anonymous memory files and the required headless environment; it returned success/513 where the dialect requires fault 7. The other findings follow directly from conflicting normative rules. I graded the embedded 0.2.2/ISA-0.8 snapshot, did not edit repositories, and did not run the full pre-flight checker.
